name: BUBBLE1-watermark-only-advanced-for-a-line-that-earns-a-bubble
why: A refused line produces nothing either way - the watermark past it buys a walk, not a law. The only difference is that a session with one system notice in the log re-reads that one line every frame for the rest of its life, which is a cost no pin can see and none here pretends to. Kept as written because the cost is real and the shape ('read forward, once') is the one a later channel tab will inherit. AUDIT NAME1 re-aimed the record at the `seq = line.seq;` line alone, which the F6 fix moved the rest of. CHAT-CHAN read every tab through the same shape and re-aimed the mutant at the one-argument law: a refused line is gathered again by the walk back from each tab's end, refused again, and draws nothing.

name: AUDIT-NAME1-F5-seen-waits-out-a-hold-of-its-own
why: A stamp left behind on a SEEN answer is never read: the return is `e.raw && ...`, and `raw` is false for exactly as long as the stale stamp exists - and the next blocked answer re-stamps it anyway, because `e.raw` is false at that moment. Written as `: null` because a field that is only correct by the grace of another field's value is the kind of thing the next hand gets wrong.
